etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English incorrigible, from Middle French incorrigible (1334), or directly from Latin incorrigibilis (“not to be corrected”), from in- (“not”) +‎ corrigere (“to correct”) +‎ -ibilis (“-able”), equivalent to in- +‎ corrigible. Recorded since 1340.
senses: Defective and impossible to materially correct or set aright.
Unmanageable; impervious to correction by punishment or pain.
